proposed_from.topic: Complete common-basal SI-PAG orientation under selection and unknown-target soft interventions. On Dai et al.'s finite causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection twin-graph class, with oracle observational and regime MAGs, construct a fixed D,K-independent sound within/cross-regime endpoint-rule calculus whose monotone closure equals the canonical endpoint-invariance SI-PAG. Prove every residual circle has opposing realizations from two compatible models sharing one basal selected DAG, and derive polynomially many oracle-input endpoint updates plus simultaneous finite-alphabet CI/invariance-test confidence SI-PAGs under positivity and a separation margin. A global basal-DAG enumerator may certify lemmas but cannot be the headline calculus. Consumer: Dai et al.'s sciPlex2/A549 perturbation analysis, where completeness determines whether remaining circles are biological ambiguity or missing orientations. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Conditional on a feasible ancestral selected set A, preserving basal edges outside E[A] and replacing E[A] by either no edge or one acyclic signature-monotone path preserves all regime skeletons and unshielded colliders. This yields exact selected-selected endpoint witnesses: an arrowhead exactly under intervention membership, and a tail when unaffected or reachable in the signature-monotone selected graph. Exhaustive checks covered 2,664 erasures, 21,312 two-regime families, 102,912 arrow witnesses, 68,160 tail witnesses, 2,997 independent twin projections, and seeded D=4 families without failure; a D=3,K=4 example forces a bidirected triangle only after cross-regime coupling. No checked source proves the common-basal completeness theorem, and v1's global enumerator remains excluded. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Lift the fixed-A construction across unknown selected sets and common exterior DAG completions using a fixed local rule list, preserving every regime fill edge and collider signature without a global realizability query. EARLY KILL TEST: Compare the explicit rule list with exact endpoint invariance on all normalized D<=3,K<=2 families, the D=3,K=4 bidirected-triangle witness, and bounded D=4,K=3 cases with varying A; for each residual circle construct both witnesses without guessing A or querying global feasibility. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest result is Dai et al. (ICLR 2025): Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7 define the fixed-model semantics, while Theorem 3 and p. 8, lines 646--662, prove soundness and explicitly leave CDIS completeness unresolved. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, is the closest fixed-calculus completeness result, but it concerns one observational PAG rather than a common-basal regime family. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and public abstract at lines 5--9 describe a known-target procedure that obtains completeness by compatible-MAG enumeration; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so no formula-level comparison is asserted. The strict gap is a fixed finite observable endpoint calculus for the unknown-target common-basal fiber, plus whole-family opposing witnesses for every residual circle. The fixed-\(A(\eta)\) signature-monotone frontier is the supporting theorem that separates this kernel from observational PAG completeness.
